1.why: 13, 18, 23 is an arithmetic run with d=5 and 11 the lone outlier; 18 sits at its middle.

2.why: 53, 81, 109 is an arithmetic run with d=28 centred on 81, which is also the only perfect square in the set.

3.why: 12 is the derivational hub - 12x3=36, 12-3=9, 12+5=17 - and it is the smaller member of the 12/36 multiple pair.

4.why: 4, 7, 13, 15 shows no run, no multiple and no sum relation; nothing separates them.

5.why: 44 = 4 x 11 is the only structural relation, and I bet the smaller member of a multiple pair is the key and the multiple is the forgot-to-divide bait.

6.why: 20, 25, 6, 32 has no run or multiple; 6 is only a magnitude outlier, which I do not treat as a key tell.

7.why: A complete sign x magnitude grid (+-2, +-9) - every cell is matched, so nothing is distinguishable.

8.why: Half the set carries a sqrt, so the source relation is quadratic in t and the key must be one of the two sqrt cells, but 2s/a vs s/(2a) inside that half is a coin flip.

9.why: Complete 2x2 grid {12x, 8x} x {-23, -11}; all four cells present, no cell distinguishable.

10.why: 4, 6, 7, 15 gives no arithmetic or geometric run and no derivational link.

11.why: Complete 2x2 grid {6, 12} x {+3/2 x, -3/2 x}; componentwise midpoint (9, 0) is absent, so no midpoint leak either.

12.why: Complete 2x2 grid {6, 8} x {x^4, x^9}; 8x^9 is faintly self-consistent as (2x^3)^3 but that is not a structural separation.

13.why: Complete 2x2 grid {>, <} x {4, -4}; nothing distinguishes a cell.

14.why: Closed group A, -A, 1/A, -1/A; the two (3 - x) cells read as sign-flip variants, leaving A and D at 50/50.

15.why: 16, 24, 32 is an arithmetic run with d=8 and 15 the lone outlier; 24 is its middle (and also the midpoint of the 16/32 doubling).

16.why: 632 is the only non-round value among three round ones; I bet the odd-formatted value is the computed key and the round ones are quantities lifted from the stem.

17.why: 16 = 2 x 8 is the only relation present; same directional bet as item 5, the smaller member is the key.

18.why: Two competing runs (5,6,7 with outlier 9; 5,7,9 with outlier 6) cancel the run tell; I took the wider-span run's middle as the less accidental of the two.

19.why: 23, 25, 27 is an arithmetic run with d=2 and 15 the lone outlier; 25 is its middle.

20.why: The pair {7, 12} appears as both the coefficients and the x-exponents, and 7 = 3+4 while 12 = 3x4, so one cell is the consistent multiply-coefficients / add-exponents cell and the grid is not really complete.

21.why: -3, 1, 5 is an arithmetic run with d=4 and -5 the lone outlier; 1 is its middle.

22.why: The factor 2 in half the options implies a 1/2 in the source formula so the key is one of the 2A/h cells, but +b2 vs -b2 within that half is a coin flip.

23.why: 27.5 is the only decimal among three integers; same directional bet as item 16, the odd-formatted value is the key.

24.why: 12 divides both 48 and 72; the hub is ambiguous between 12 and 48, and I applied the smaller-member direction from item 5.

25.why: 9, 13, 20, 37 gives no run, no multiple, no pair sum to a supplied constant.

26.why: 24 = 3 x 8 is the only relation; the smaller-member direction picks 8, though here it conflicts with 8 also being the magnitude outlier.

27.why: Complete reciprocal x sign grid (+-2, +-1/2); no cell is distinguishable.

28.why: 11, 12, 13, 14 is a full consecutive block with no outlier, so not even a run tell; a central value is the weakest possible lean.
